purpose: Chlordiazepoxide is used to help relieve anxiety and nervousness. It is also commonly used to help people safely withdraw from alcohol by reducing shaking, agitation, and seizure risk. Sometimes doctors prescribe it for short-term relief of tension or irritable bowel symptoms.
how_it_works: Your brain has a natural calming chemical called GABA. Chlordiazepoxide boosts the effect of that calming chemical, which slows down overactive nerve signals in your brain. This helps you feel less anxious, more relaxed, and reduces the chance of seizures during alcohol withdrawal.
common_side_effects: Feeling drowsy or sleepy, dizziness, feeling unsteady or clumsy, confusion, blurred vision, nausea, and constipation. These effects are often stronger when you first start taking it.
warnings: This medicine can be habit-forming, so do not take more than prescribed and do not stop it suddenly without talking to your doctor — stopping abruptly can cause dangerous withdrawal. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medication, as it can cause extreme drowsiness or dangerous breathing problems. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have liver, kidney, or breathing problems.
typical_dosing: For anxiety, a typical adult dose is 5 to 25 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day. For alcohol withdrawal, doses may be higher and are closely supervised by a doctor. Older adults usually start at lower doses to reduce the risk of falls and confusion. Always take exactly as your doctor tells you.
